---
title: "Download"
subtitle: "Find and download the products with fesmdata.jl"
---

The products are downloaded with `fesmdata.jl`, a Julia script of FesmData, which puts
every file in a fixed layout and checks it against its checksum. Single files can also be
downloaded without it (see [Single files](#single-files)).

## Get the tool

You need [Julia](https://julialang.org/downloads/) (a recent version; no packages to
install) and a copy of FesmData. All commands are run from its folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fesmc/FesmData.git
cd FesmData
julia fesmdata.jl help
```

`git pull` updates it, and with it the list of the released products.

## Where the data go

The environment variable `FESMDATA` sets the folder for the data, e.g. in your
`~/.bashrc`:

```bash
export FESMDATA=/path/to/fesmdata
```

The products go to `$FESMDATA/products` (or to `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS`, if set). On
Levante and Albedo, `source shared/machines/<machine>.env` sets it to the shared folder
of the project, where the products usually are already (see
[Machines and storage](machines.qmd)). On macOS or Windows, do not put it next to the
FesmData folder as `fesmdata`: on a case-insensitive file system, that is FesmData
itself.

Every file goes to `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS/<Domain>/<GRID>/`: one folder per domain, and in
it one folder per grid with all datasets on that grid. A grid folder thus holds
everything a model needs on that grid, and can be copied as a whole:

```
$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS/
  Antarctica/
    ANT-8KM/
      grid_ANT-8KM.txt                 grid description (cdo)
      ANT-8KM_grid.nc                  x, y, lon, lat and area of the cells
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-BedMachine-v4.nc    a product of the dataset Topo
      ANT-8KM_TOPO-Bedmap3.nc
      ANT-8KM_GHF-Lucazeau2019.nc      a product of the dataset GHF
      ...
    ANT-16KM/
  Greenland/
    GRL-4KM/
  ...
  Records/
    IceCores/
      IceCores-Kindler2014.nc          a product of the records dataset IceCores
      IceCores-Kindler2014.txt         its text form
```

Domains are named after their folder (Antarctica, Greenland, Thwaites, Patagonia, ...),
grids after the key of their domain and their resolution (ANT-8KM, GRL-500M, DDG-25M);
a grid name thus also gives its domain. See [Domains](domains.qmd) for all domains and
grids, and [Products](products.qmd) for what is released on each.

## Find what is there

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl list                     # all released datasets on all domains
julia fesmdata.jl list Topo                # a dataset on all its domains (or a domain)
julia fesmdata.jl list Antarctica Topo     # a dataset on a domain: its grids and
                                           # files, their sizes, and which are here
julia fesmdata.jl list ANT-8KM             # everything on a grid
```

The arguments can be given in any order. `list` also shows the products that nests and
crops get by cropping (see [Nests and crops](#nests-and-crops)).

To find products by what they are rather than by dataset, `search` looks for terms in
the names of the products and their files, their sources (with the titles, authors and
references of their READMEs), their variables (where the definitions list them) and the
domains they are released on, ignoring case and accents; a product must contain all
terms:

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl search Montoya           # the products from Montoya and Levermann (2008)
julia fesmdata.jl search ghf Antarctica    # heat flow products released on Antarctica
```

Products not released yet are listed too, as `(not released)`.

## Download what you need

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM            # one grid
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Topo ANT-8KM ANT-16KM   # several grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch Antarctica Topo         # all grids of a domain
julia fesmdata.jl fetch IceCores Records        # a records dataset
```

`fetch` needs the dataset, and a domain or grids (in any order). A grid name implies its
domain, so the domain can be left out when grids are given.

`path` prints the paths of the downloaded files of a dataset, one per line, for scripts
and viewers; products can be named to keep only theirs (the files missing are counted
on stderr):

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl path Topo ANT-8KM                  # all products of Topo on a grid
ncview $(julia fesmdata.jl path Topo ANT-8KM BedMachine-v4)
```

## Nests and crops

The thematic datasets (those made by remapping: GHF, Velocity, SMB, Atmosphere, ...)
are released once, on the domain or crop that has them, and not again on the nests and
crops inside it (e.g. Thwaites, a crop of Antarctica, or Jakobshavn, a nest of
GreenlandPaleo inside its crop Greenland); a nest or crop is released with its own
products only (e.g. Topo, Regions). `fetch` makes the others there on demand, by cropping
them:

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl list Jakobshavn          # its datasets, and those by cropping
julia fesmdata.jl list Jakobshavn SMB      # the grids and files that fetch makes
julia fesmdata.jl fetch SMB Jakobshavn     # all grids
julia fesmdata.jl fetch SMB JAK-4KM        # one grid
```

A nest or crop gets, for each thematic dataset, its own products; those of its parent
domain that it does not have; and those of the crops of its parent domain that contain
it (e.g. Greenland for the nests of GreenlandPaleo: MAR, Joughin2018, ...) that neither
has (`list` shows where each comes from). `fetch` downloads the files of these products
(e.g. Greenland/SMB, to `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS/Greenland/`), and cuts each to the nest or
crop, as `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS/<Domain>/<GRID>/<GRID>_<NAME>.nc` with the grid files:

- at a resolution of the nest or crop, on its own grid (e.g. JAK-1KM, next to its Topo
  and Regions, whose grid files it takes);
- at the other resolutions, on the cells of the domain grids that overlap the nest or
  crop (e.g. JAK-4KM, the same cells from the parent and from a crop, which lie on the
  parent grids).

A grid of a crop that does not cover the nest or crop is skipped, with a message (no
partial crops). The crops are exact subsets of the files they are cut from (all
variables, attributes and compression as they are), and record that file and its cells
in their global attributes (`cropped_from`, `cropped_from_checksum`,
`cropped_from_release`, `cropped_index_xc` and `cropped_index_yc`, 1-based). Running
`fetch` again keeps the crops of the current files, and makes them again after a new
release. A grid of the nest or crop whose released files are on another grid than in
`shared/domains.toml` (a release made before the grid changed) stops the cropping, until
it is released again. Cropping needs a few Julia packages (NCDatasets, FesmUtils), which
`fetch` installs on first use.

## Mirror everything

To keep a copy of all products on a machine (or of a dataset or a domain):

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl mirror                # everything
julia fesmdata.jl mirror Topo           # one dataset
julia fesmdata.jl mirror Antarctica     # one domain
```

It first checks the files present, shows what is to download or update and its size,
and asks once. Run it again after new releases to update the copy: only new and changed
files are downloaded (`--yes` skips the question, e.g. in a job). `mirror` also makes
the products of the active nests and crops by cropping (as `fetch`, see
[Nests and crops](#nests-and-crops)), e.g. Stratigraphy on Greenland from GreenlandPaleo;
crops already made from the current files are kept.

## Archives and other folders

`--dir=<folder>` lists, fetches or mirrors in `<folder>/<Domain>/<GRID>/` instead of
`$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS` (`FESMDATA` need not be set); `fetch --dir` writes the crops there
too. Only the latest release of each dataset is kept on Helmholtz Codebase, so to keep
the releases in use before updating, mirror them into a folder first:

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl mirror --dir=/work/ba1442/fesmdata/archive/2026-10-12
julia fesmdata.jl mirror
```

Files already in `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS` at the same release (checksums) are hard linked
from there (no extra space; copied on another file system, or with `--copy`), the others
downloaded, and the registry files of the released datasets go to `<folder>/registry/`,
as the list of what the folder holds. Updates of `$FESMDATA_PRODUCTS` write new files,
so the hard links keep the archived ones; tools that change files in place (e.g.
`ncatted`) would change both: use `--copy` for an archive next to files that may be
changed in place. Running `mirror --dir` again on an archive updates it to the latest
releases. Earlier releases still in use are kept in such archives on the HPC systems.

## Checksums and updates

Every file is checked against its checksum (sha256) after download. Files already
present are kept if they are of the release, and replaced if they are of an earlier
release (`fetch` and `mirror` update them); a file changed locally (not of a release)
stops the download, unless `--overwrite` is given.

## Versions and citation

Each release of a dataset has a version (e.g. Topo 2.2.0, tag `topo-v2.2.0` of
FesmData), shown on the [Products](products.qmd) page and by `list`. Every file records
how it was made in its global attributes (`fesmdata_version`, `fesmdata_commit`,
`history`), and the sources it was made from. Please cite the original datasets (see the
page of each dataset), and the DOI of the release where there is one (releases can be
archived on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/communities/fesmc)). `cite` shows where the
references of products are: the README of each source (references and licence), the
README of the dataset, and the DOIs of the releases:

```bash
julia fesmdata.jl cite Paleoclimate CLIMBER3a-present   # one product (or several)
julia fesmdata.jl cite GHF                              # all products of a dataset
```

## Single files {#single-files}

Single files can also be downloaded without the tool, from the end of the page of each
dataset (Downloads) or from
[Helmholtz Codebase](https://codebase.helmholtz.cloud/fesmc/fesmdata-products/-/packages),
one package per domain, dataset and grid. Download the grid files of the grid too
(`grid_<GRID>.txt`, `<GRID>_grid.nc`).
